translation_direction: de → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete German electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Narration: chàng for Gregor, người cha / người mẹ; Gregor’s inner speech mình, tôi aloud to the chief clerk, con to his parents; the family uses bố/mẹ/con and Grete anh/em.
decisions.rationale: Standardised across three separately drafted parts.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Grete’s pronoun shift for Gregor (es → er in ‘er fängt schon wieder an’ and over the corpse in 3.31) had been flattened to nó; now anh ấy where she says er, nó where she says es.
Cross-part consistency: tàu điện (2.2/3.38); the father’s self-reference bố (2.29); Kommis as nhân viên bán hàng (3.7).
Grete’s ‘Du, Gregor!’ restored as a threat (Anh… Gregor!); the mother’s ‘Mọi người’ (2.19); Endlich as Thế là xong! (3.28).
Calques fixed: der große Schnitt (1.5), verfolgen (1.18), sich aussöhnen (3.9), Doppelkinn (2.29), Dienermütze (3.19); the lieutenant’s quân phục (1.26); German-style ‘–,’ punctuation removed.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: con sâu bọ khổng lồ / con quái vật / con vật / con bọ hung
glossary.rationale: Distinct words for Kafka’s distinct terms, never conflated.
Grete’s deliberate shift from es to er, and back to er over the corpse, is mirrored.

glossary.draft_rendering: ông chánh văn phòng / bà giúp việc / ba ông thuê trọ / ghế xô-pha / đi-văng
đồng phục (father) / chế phục; quân phục for the lieutenant
glossary.rationale: Keeps Kafka’s military/servile and Uniform/Livree distinctions.

witness_decision: Selected the complete text of Die Verwandlung (Leipzig: Kurt Wolff Verlag, 1917; Der jüngste Tag 22/23) as transcribed in Project Gutenberg #22367. First published in Die weißen Blätter, October 1915, and as a book in 1915; not collated.

unresolved_questions.explanation: Endlich! as Thế là xong! keeps the release but loses some of the sense of ‘at last’.

title_review.rationale: Hóa thân is the established, sober Vietnamese title and matches cuộc hóa thân in the text; it avoids the more sensational Biến dạng.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Compared part I: the waking, the chief clerk and the father’s driving Gregor back.
Compared part II: feeding, the furniture, the picture and the apple.
Compared part III: the lodgers, the violin, the verdict, the death and the ending.
